headings.text: Channel B — environment packages via device profile
What standard sources are — and are not — for

blocks.html:
⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. The opendefense-platform is under breaking development; verify against the code before relying on details.

Enrol any client through RASENMAEHER and it wakes up with the Finnish MML basemaps — Peruskartta and Ortoilmakuva, plus the Google set — already in its map switcher, without anyone touching the Import tool. This page dissects how that works and how to make your own layer equally automatic: a standard data source that every deployment hands to every client out of the box. Notably, nothing in the opendefense-platform repo defines the MML maps — they ship inside the takrmapi image (ghcr.io/pvarki/tak-integration, built from pvarki/python-tak-rmapi) through two separate channels.

Channel A — the enrollment zip

When takrmapi builds a client's onboarding package (the client-zip endpoint — see Enrolling & getting a client certificate), it renders the template tree src/takrmapi/templates/tak_missionpkg/default/ — one folder per client variant: atak, itak, wintak, tak-tracker. Each folder holds server.pref.tpl, the map-source XMLs, and a MANIFEST/manifest.xml.tpl that lists them. Whatever sits in the variant folder and has a manifest line lands in every new client's zip.

The map sources themselves are nothing exotic — plain ATAK <customMapSource> XYZ tile definitions. MML_Peruskartta.xml declares "1 MML Peruskartta" at https://tiles.kartat.kapsi.fi/peruskartta/{$z}/{$x}/{$y}.jpg, zoom 2–19; MML_Ortoilmakuva.xml points at the same host's ortokuva path. That is Maanmittauslaitos raster served via the kapsi.fi community mirror, not MML directly — worth knowing before you bet an exercise on its availability.

Channel B — environment packages via device profile

At startup, takrmapi's setup_tak_defaults() (takutils/tak_init.py) creates the **Default-ATAK** connection profile in TAK Server with apply_on_connect=true, and uploads into it zips built from templates/tak_datapackage/default/environment-packages/. Which folders become zips is hard-coded in config.py as TAK_DATAPACKAGE_ADDON_FOLDER_ZIP_PACKAGES; the set includes Maps, carrying the same MML/Google XMLs plus a Map_defaults.pref. Every client that connects receives these packages automatically — the enrollment zip's server.pref sets deviceProfileEnableOnConnect=true, so ATAK asks for the profile on connect.

The two channels are deliberate belt-and-braces: the zip gives a brand-new client its maps before it ever reaches the server; the profile catches every client that connects — including ones enrolled before a package existed. Both channels also set eud_api_sync_mapsources=false (in server.pref and Map_defaults.pref respectively), so clients do not pull map sources from TAK's own EUD sync API — these two paths are the delivery mechanism, full stop.

blocks.html:
Adding your own source

The upstream route — the one that makes a source standard for everyone. In python-tak-rmapi, add MySource.xml plus its manifest line under both template trees: each client-variant folder in tak_missionpkg/default/ (and its manifest.xml.tpl), and the Maps folder in tak_datapackage/default/environment-packages/. Miss a variant folder and iTAK/WinTAK users silently go without. Rebuild ghcr.io/pvarki/tak-integration, then bump the tag in both overlays:

# k8s/app-tak/overlays/{local,cloud}/kustomization.yaml
images:
- name: tak-rmapi-image
  newName: ghcr.io/pvarki/tak-integration
  newTag: 1.14.3-260822   # <- your rebuilt tag

The platform-side route — no fork required. takrmapi's config.py settings are env-overridable with the TI_ prefix, and the overlays already merge literals into takrmapi-config via a configMapGenerator. Point the template folders at your own tree, mounted from a ConfigMap:

configMapGenerator:
- name: takrmapi-config
  behavior: merge
  literals:
  - TI_TAK_MISSIONPKG_TEMPLATES_FOLDER=/custom-templates/tak_missionpkg
  - TI_TAK_DATAPACKAGE_TEMPLATES_FOLDER=/custom-templates/tak_datapackage

Two caveats make this less pleasant than it looks. First, you own the whole tree: takrmapi reads only the folder you point it at, so you must replicate every stock file — server.pref.tpl, all four variant folders, the manifests — and you stop receiving upstream template fixes. Second, TAK_DATAPACKAGE_ADDON_FOLDER_ZIP_PACKAGES is hard-coded, not env-overridable — you can change what is inside the existing packages (Maps), but adding a brand-new environment-package zip needs the upstream route.

The dedupe trap

Device-profile uploads dedupe by file name. Ship changed content under the same Maps.zip and an existing deployment never re-pushes it — clients keep the old sources indefinitely. Either give the package folder a new name (an upstream change, since the folder list is hard-coded), or delete the stale file from the Default-ATAK profile in TAK so the next takrmapi startup uploads it fresh.

What standard sources are — and are not — for

Standard sources are for slow-changing content: basemaps and reference layers that should exist on day one and rarely change, because every change rides an image rebuild or a template-tree edit plus the dedupe dance above. Anything dynamic — refreshing weather grids, live overlays, anything on a cron — belongs in mission packages published over the Marti API instead; that loop is covered in Publishing data programmatically in this chapter, and demonstrated end-to-end by the scripts/dronewx pipeline.
